response.title: I'm switching my 36 volt golf cart from lead-acid to lithium. What else do I need to buy besides the battery to make it work?
response.answer:
Converting a 36V golf cart from lead-acid to lithium (LiFePO4) is usually pretty straightforward. You can typically keep your existing motor, controller, and most of the wiring.

However, there are a few additional components you'll need, and some depend on your cart's make and model.

What you'll need besides the lithium battery

Component

	

Required?

	

Why you need it




36V lithium battery charger

	

Yes

	

Your old lead-acid charger generally isn't compatible with lithium batteries.




Battery cables and terminals

	

Maybe

	

Your existing cables may work, but the lithium battery may have different terminals or positioning.




Battery mounting brackets or straps

	

Yes, if not included

	

Secures the smaller lithium battery in the existing battery compartment.




36V-to-12V voltage reducer

	

Depends

	

Needed if your lights, horn, or accessories require 12V and don't already have a suitable power supply.




Lithium-compatible battery gauge

	

Recommended

	

Your old lead-acid charge indicator may give inaccurate readings.




Main battery fuse or circuit breaker

	

Recommended

	

Protects the battery wiring against short circuits. Must be properly rated for DC voltage and fault current.




Solenoid or controller upgrade

	

Usually no

	

Most stock 36V carts can retain these components, provided the battery and BMS are compatible.

The most important thing: battery current rating

Don't choose a lithium battery based only on its voltage and amp-hour capacity.

Your battery's Battery Management System (BMS) must be able to handle the current your golf cart draws, especially when accelerating or climbing hills.

For example, a battery advertised as 36V 100Ah might have a 100A BMS, which could be insufficient for some golf carts.

Check the battery's continuous discharge rating, peak discharge rating, and how its BMS handles temporary overloads. These must match your cart's motor and controller requirements.

Two things that may be specific to your cart

Charging port or onboard computer: Some carts require a charger receptacle adapter, interlock wiring changes, or a charging-system bypass. This is particularly relevant to certain older Club Car models.

12V accessories: If your existing lights were powered by tapping part of the lead-acid battery bank, that arrangement needs to change when installing a single lithium pack. 
CartVolts
+1

I would look for a complete 36V LiFePO4 golf cart conversion kit with a matched charger, battery monitor, cables, and mounting hardware. It often makes the conversion easier than purchasing everything separately.

Let me narrow down exactly what you need

What is the make, model, and year of your golf cart?

For example:

E-Z-GO TXT, 2005

Club Car DS, 1998

Yamaha G2, 1990

Also, are you planning to install one large 36V lithium battery, or multiple smaller lithium batteries?

With those details, I can tell you which additional parts are actually necessary and which ones you can skip.
